question: Does the disputed word-initial on Turku fragment C resemble nearby d or r forms?
physical_location: Left writing field; the catalogue calls it folio 1v. Select second viewer image manually, because deep links reset in this session.
exposure: Same AI had already seen target, 2017 TEI and external dedisti concordance. Controls chosen after that exposure; this is not an independent, blind or preregistered palaeographic assessment.

regions.name: word-initial positive controls
regions.location: Upper part of left field, line containing candidate dominum deum nostrum
regions.observation: The candidate word-initial d forms have a bowl with a tall oblique ascender, broadly similar to the disputed initial. The surrounding words and expansion of their abbreviated forms are reference-assisted.

regions.name: neighboring d and r controls and target
regions.location: Lower left field, adjacent lines containing candidate benedictus fructus ventris tui and Sicut mirra electa odorem ...
regions.observation: The disputed initial, the d in odorem and the d in candidate benedictus appear to share a bowl and tall oblique ascender. The r forms in candidate fructus and ventris look shorter, without the same obvious ascender. The last strokes of the disputed word remain faded.

caveats: The comparison reuses the same viewer image and AI reader; it is not a new manuscript witness or independent confirmation.
Word position, adjacent letters, abbreviation and script variants can affect letter shape; the selected r controls are not exact position-matched initial r controls.
No quantitative glyph classification or blinded selection was performed.
A concordance supports dedisti as a familiar chant wording but cannot supply any illegible Turku letters.
The page's transcription policy and first notice of a possible error remain unknown.
conclusion: The local d/r controls strengthen the provisional reading d as the word's first character. The catalogue's redisti is a plausible transcription error and dedisti a plausible proposed reading; keep the ending and correction unconfirmed pending independent review.
classification: B: plausible, unreviewed modern transcription correction
